title: Consumption of Fermented Versus Unfermented Milk Products in Adulthood: Impact on Protein Synthesis, Gut Microbiome, and Cardiovascular Health
content: Milk evolved to support growth of newborn mammals, but consumption in adulthood can shape health benefits. Aim: To examine health consequences of adults’ consumption of dairy including (1) of milk proteins’ effect on muscle hypertrophy (MHT) when combined with resistance exercise training (RET); (2) of fermented milk products and probiotics on gut microbiome (GM), and (3) of saturated milkfat on cardiovascular health (CVH), in cohort and randomized controlled trial studies. Findings: (1) Whey and casein modestly augment, but are not essential, relative to plant proteins, for RET-associated MHT. (2) Fermented dairy products and probiotics beneficially affect GM and overall health. (3) Cardiovascular risks of milkfat are mitigated by bioactive constituents of dairy matrices, fermentation, and lowering of its saturation, features that are reduced or absent, along with cardiovascular benefits, in butter. Conclusions. Knowledge gaps regarding lifelong consumption of dairy products require identification of bioactivities of their nutrient matrices, their links to atherogenic lipoproteins, and definition of risk-free thresholds for adult consumption. Such research would promote precision nutrition toward mitigation of some metabolic disabilities and promotion of better health. Overall, milk products represent a healthy natural source of nutrition but need to be prudently controlled for safe lifelong consumption in adulthood.
